subject: DPA negotiation: conditional erase & region safeguards (Aurora Health)

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@aurorahealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: Data handling and erase conditions — draft redlines

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is Aurora's v3 redline of the DPA (high level asks below). Legal is looping in our outside counsel (Andrew) for any statutory interpretation, but we wanted to flag the commercial items up front:

- Residency: we need explicit onshore processing for PHI-derived payloads where state law requires it; would accept a committed region (US) with a carve-in for state-level requirements.
- Deletion: ask is immediate erase of customer data on termination + certification within 30 days; we would like an explicit exception for backups to be destroyed no later than 90 days after termination.
- Evidence: request a signed deletion certificate and summary of steps taken (keys destroyed, backup lifecycle actions).
- Legal hold: require Redwood to preserve data when Aurora issues a written hold; want scope and notice window spelled out.

We attached a version with inline comments. Can your team confirm which points Redwood can accept as-is and which will require counter-language? Also please call out any operational constraints (snapshots, immutable backups, third-party backups).

Apologies in advance for the redlines — we tried to be narrow.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement
Aurora Health

Attachment: Aurora_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx (document, 42KB)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: Data handling and erase conditions — draft redlines

Maria — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. High-level reaction and proposed next steps: 

1) Residency: Redwood can commit to US-only processing for workloads Aurora designates as "sensitive" (PHI-derived) provided Aurora supplies the list of tenants/environments to lock to US regions. We propose language that permits transient cross-region replication for disaster recovery but requires primary processing and storage in US regions unless a documented exception is requested.

2) Deletion timeline: we can provide a certification of deletion and run our erase workflow. Operationally, snapshot and immutable backup media sometimes require a short retention window — we are comfortable with a 90-day maximum backup retention after termination for production backups. For logs/telemetry we propose a separate retention (30 days by default) unless you require longer for audit.

3) Evidence: we can provide a deletion certificate and an audit log export showing erase operations. We can commit to delivering the certificate within 7 business days after completion of the erase run.

4) Legal hold: we need a defined process (written notice to security@redwood.ai with hold ID and scope). We suggest Redwood will suspend normal erasure for the named datasets for the duration of the hold and will notify Aurora of impacted retention. We propose that Aurora reimburse extraordinary preservation costs if hold extends beyond 90 days.

I'll loop in Priyom with the technical appendix and Laura for legal wording. Can we aim for a follow-up call Friday to go over the proposed paragraph-level language? Also, Maria — would you share the specific state statutes you're most concerned about so we can confirm operational feasibility?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-erase-playbook.pdf (summary of operational erase steps, 120KB)

Subject: Fwd: technical appendix for erase/backups (internal)

Karthik / Laura — forwarding a compact technical appendix we drafted to support the response. Key operational details (summary):

- Primary storage: per-tenant region pinning (US only) supported via deployment tag; replication to a secondary US region only for DR.
- Backups: snapshots are immutable for 14 days, after which they become soft-deletable; cold backup copies to third-party cloud object storage have a 90-day max retention post-termination.
- Wiping: KMS key rotation combined with object-level deletion is our standard proof-of-deletion playbook — we can produce key-rotation logs + object deletion manifests as evidence.
- Logs: audit logs are stored for 30 days by default (configurable up to 1 year).

Notes/asks for legal: we should not promise sub-30-day certification timelines for very large datasets without a carveout (network egress limits and customer-specified export can cause delays). 7 business days for the certificate is reasonable for typical cases.

Karthik / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the appendix. A few clarifications from our side after counsel review: 

- Absolute max: Aurora prefers the DPA to state the 90-day max for backups as a mandatory limit (not just an operational practice). Can Redwood accept a contractual "no backups retained beyond 90 days post-termination" clause?
- Certificate content: our legal counsel requires that the deletion certificate list KMS key identifiers and the deletion manifest (object IDs or snapshot IDs) to the extent Redwood can provide them. If any of that is redacted for security, please specify what will be shared.
- State carve-outs: we are asking for an exception for states with express data localization statutes that require onshore processing of certain personal health data. We are happy to provide a short list of those statutes.

If we can get affirmative language on the 90-day absolute max and an itemized list of what appears on the deletion certificate, I think counsel will be comfortable moving forward. We are ready to proceed to DocuSign once the redlines are in place.

Thanks,
Maria

Maria / Andrew — appreciate the clarity. After internal sync (Priyom + Laura + Grace), here's a consolidated counterproposal that tries to meet Aurora's legal asks while preserving operational accuracy: 

1) 90-day backup cap: Redwood accepts a firm contractual commitment that no customer data backups will be retained beyond 90 days post-termination. We will define "backups" in the DPA to include snapshots, immutable snapshot copies, and third-party backup exports. Operational note: we will implement the policy via our backup lifecycle and will provide a deletion schedule as evidence.

2) Deletion certificate: Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate within 7 business days of erase completion. The certificate will include: dataset identifier(s), deletion timestamp(s), KMS key IDs used to encrypt the deleted objects (where available), and a deletion manifest listing snapshot IDs and object prefixes removed. If any KMS details are restricted due to key sanitation, we will provide a hashed reference and the key rotation record.

3) State carve-outs: Redwood will accept a limited carve-out for jurisdictions that legally require onshore processing. Aurora to supply the statute list; Redwood will evaluate each and propose an implementation timeline and an exception process. Any additional cost for region-specific deployment (e.g., dedicated onshore tenancy) will be handled as a commercial addendum.

4) Legal hold process: Aurora must submit a written hold request to security@redwood.ai with the hold scope and duration. Redwood will suspend erasure for the specified datasets for the duration of the hold and will notify Aurora of any preservation cost exposure after 90 days.

Next steps: Laura will produce paragraph-level language for each of the above and attach a tracked-redline within 48 hours. If Aurora confirms the statute list and accepts the 90-day delete cap as written, we can finalize and route to DocuSign (I'll send a link).

Proposed call: Wed 18 Jan 2028 11:00 AM PT to close any remaining items. Does that work on your side?
